title: NNTP reader: NNTPS implicit TLS on port 563; remove STARTTLS upgrade path
description: STARTTLS is a compatibility hack from when TLS was not the default. This project is greenfield; do it right. Design: listen on two ports. Port 119 (plaintext): no TLS upgrade, no auth — AUTHINFO returns 483 unconditionally if auth.required=true. Port 563 (NNTPS): TLS from the first byte, full AUTHINFO available. Config: add tls.addr (e.g. '0.0.0.0:563') alongside the existing listen.addr for plaintext. When tls.addr is set, the TcpListener for it is wrapped with tokio-rustls acceptor before any NNTP bytes are exchanged. Implementation: remove the run_plain_session STARTTLS upgrade loop, remove starttls_available from SessionContext, remove Command::StartTls (or return 502 for compat). The session code becomes simpler: run_tls_session and run_plain_session are distinguished only by which port the connection arrived on, not by mid-session state. SMTP note: port 465 (SMTPS, implicit TLS) is the right answer for submission too — file separately as SMTP STARTTLS is unavoidable on port 25 for MTA-to-MTA.
notes: STARTTLS is already implemented in the reader (lifecycle.rs). This issue only adds the enforcement: if starttls_available and !is_tls, return 483 on AUTHINFO USER. No new STARTTLS work needed — 1c8.8 is unblocked.
